questions.question: What is the typical progression of fine-tuning techniques from simplest to most advanced?
questions.explanation: The standard progression is Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) with labeled examples, then RLHF (Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback) for alignment, and finally DPO (Direct Preference Optimization) which simplifies RLHF by removing the reward model.

questions.question: What is the main advantage of DPO over traditional RLHF?
choices: DPO requires more training data than RLHF
DPO eliminates the need for a separate reward model by directly optimizing on preference data
DPO only works with text-to-image models
DPO is slower to train but produces better results
questions.explanation: DPO (Direct Preference Optimization) combines the reward modeling and RL steps into a single supervised learning objective, making it simpler, more stable, and computationally cheaper than the full RLHF pipeline.

questions.question: Why is SFT (Supervised Fine-Tuning) typically the first step before RLHF or DPO?
choices: SFT makes the model smaller and faster
SFT teaches the model the desired output format and basic task behavior, providing a strong foundation for subsequent alignment
SFT is required by law before any model deployment
SFT removes all harmful content from the model
questions.explanation: SFT on high-quality instruction-response pairs teaches the model the task format and expected behavior. Without this baseline, RLHF/DPO would struggle because the model wouldn't know the basic structure of good responses.
